topics.topic: Actor attribution for requester-driven, automatic, multi-stage, and recovery-authored records
questions: How do `functions.submit_implementation` and `flows.activate_flow_version` obtain the kernel Actor for an automatic Activation or FlowActivation while retaining the requesting owner or agent for records authored by that requester?
How does an operation invoked with an owner or agent actor obtain and record the distinct kernel actor for automatic verdicts and activations?
For every record written by a multi-stage operation, which actor is recorded, and where is that attribution stored when the State 1 model does not name an actor field?

Do TrialExecution, NodeExecution and EffectApproval records carry an initiating actor, and for advancement caused by start, resume, approval or startup recovery is that actor the current requester, the run starter or the kernel?

quotes: Every operation that writes a record receives the acting Actor M27 — owner, agent by name, or kernel — from its caller; `module:surface` determines it from the token (A16 rule 3) and nothing else names it.
judgement.why: The change did not touch this actor-attribution convention or make its application to automatic records newly material.

topics.topic: Preflight and cleanup policy for unreferenced content-addressed bytes
questions: Must every fit and fixture-size check be completed before any bytes are copied, or may a refused capture leave unreferenced content-addressed bytes?
Must all case-fit and fixture-size checks complete before copying files, or may a refused capture leave unreferenced content-addressed bytes?
Must `runs.capture_failed_execution` preflight every `functions.add_captured_trial_case` check before copying files, or may a later refusal leave unreferenced copied bytes?
Are complete content-addressed bytes with no owning StoredValue or TrialCase deliberately retained, removed immediately, or collected at startup?

quotes: `runs` copies a spooled file into the content-addressed area only after every check of the capture has passed on the records and the files' facts — eligibility, run and spool, then the input fits and sizes `functions.add_captured_trial_case` would make —, so a refused capture copies nothing and owner decision 9 holds: the only files kept beyond a run are trial-case fixtures.

Cleanup duty: capture copies files before the run's spool can go; files copied before `module:functions` refuses the case stay in the content-addressed area, named by no record (State 3, "Bytes left by a refused capture"); release is the only removal of a failed run's spool, and the content-addressed copy of a captured file is the only file that outlives its run (K-10).
judgement.why: State 3 requires all checks before copying and says a refusal copies nothing, while State 4 permits copied bytes to remain after a refusal.

topics.topic: Validation and first-failure ordering of pre-send request checks
questions: What is the exact first-failure order among missing instance, invalid or missing address, disallowed plain HTTP, repeated required headers and invalid required headers?

What is the complete first-failure order among `instance_not_selected`, `instance_address_missing`, `plain_http_not_allowed`, `required_header_repeated`, `required_header_invalid`, `credential_unresolved` and `input_not_placeable`?
Does `prepare_request` validate required-header names and values at send time, and exactly where does `required_header_invalid` occur in its check order?

quotes: A check of the kernel's own that fails before anything is sent is done before any EffectAttempt is written. The checks run in this order and the first that fails is named: the binding is stale or no longer invocable (A08 rule 6); the instance or its address is missing or not allowed, or a required header is repeated or invalid (rules 1 and 4, A08 rule 5), or its credential cannot be resolved (A17); an input value cannot be placed in the request (rule 2).

State 3 order after the binding: no selected instance (no name) is `instance_not_selected`; no `api_base_url` (a name without one — whether the record lists no instance of that name, the instance has no `api_base_url`, or it is not an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host, A08 rule 5) is `instance_address_missing`; a repeated required header, a plain `http` target not allowed, then the credential, then input placement, input ports in name order and a list's elements in list order, the first that cannot be placed named (A09 rules 1, 2, 4, 6); credential by name only in the description (A10 rule 7); the description covers every header sent on the wire, and no header is sent that it does not describe; one `host` header, the instance's required `host` when it names one, else the authority of `api_base_url` (A10 rule 7); a `GET` or `DELETE` list input that is empty adds no query parameter (A09 rule 2).
judgement.why: A09 puts a disallowed address before repeated or invalid headers, whereas the State 5 operation puts repeated headers before disallowed plain HTTP and omits invalid-header validation from the ordered sequence.

topics.topic: Cleanup and retry semantics for spooled files after partial or later failures
questions: What must `spool_file` do when the same spool identity already exists after a previous record-change failure?
What result does `spool_file` return for a symbolic link or I/O failure, and what happens to files already spooled for that attempt?
How are files already spooled for a function attempt removed when a later output check or record write makes that attempt fail?
How are unrecorded spooled files handled after the later record transaction fails, and what happens when recovery retries the same attempt identity and finds a completed file already there?

judgement.divergence: One implementation removes or safely reuses orphaned spool files after an attempt or record transaction fails; another leaves them and may reject or corrupt a recovery retry that encounters the existing identity, which the run owner and host operator notice through different retry outcomes and retained spool usage.
judgement.why: The texts require failed-attempt files to be discarded but define neither an attempt-scoped cleanup operation nor collision and I/O behavior for already-published unrecorded spool files.

topics.topic: First-start creation and validation of store paths and database structures
questions: What must `open_store` do on the first start when some or all store paths do not yet exist?
On a first installation, which missing store paths and database structures does `open_store` create, with what permissions, and which missing paths instead stop startup?

quotes: Take the exclusive lock, check the data directory and remove temporary files before any record is read.
judgement.why: The change did not touch the first-start behavior of `open_store` or make missing store paths newly relevant.

topics.topic: Process termination after runtime store failures following state changes
questions: Which runtime `internal_error` conditions require the kernel process to terminate after answering, especially failures after an effect, spool write or earlier run change?
Must an `internal_error` after any earlier run-affecting store change stop the process so startup recovery runs before another request, and how is that requirement signalled to `surface`?

judgement.divergence: One implementation terminates the process after returning an `internal_error` whenever an earlier run-affecting change was committed, forcing startup recovery before another request; another keeps serving because only `stop_required` has an explicit termination signal, which callers and the owner notice through whether another request can run against lagging run state.
judgement.why: The required stop after a later store failure is not connected to a distinct public-operation result or to `surface`'s runtime termination behavior.

topics.topic: Record mutability and lifecycle transition storage semantics
questions: Which record types and fields are mutable in place, and does reading return the updated entity or an immutable event history?
Which records may be updated in place, and is each lifecycle transition an update of the original store position or a newly appended record?

quotes: Only `store` opens the database; records are never edited (A01 rule 6).

`store` checks only its own invariants — attempt numbers, unique and existing identities, links, no record edited — a lifecycle change (a status, who decided or resolved or released and when, `concluded_at`) updates those fields of the entity's one record in place, which keeps its store position, the position of its creation; every other field is never changed — and trusts its caller for every rule of the caller's decision.
judgement.why: One passage prohibits editing records while the other expressly requires lifecycle fields to be updated in place.

topics.topic: Schema declaration and identity semantics for flow constants
questions: Does every constant input include its own declared `value_schema` as well as its class and value, or is its schema taken from its target port?
Must each constant submission include its own `value_schema`, and is that schema part of the constant and flow-version identity even when its target port is missing?

quotes: A constant's StoredValue takes the `value_schema` and class the composing agent declared with it (State 6, decision 5), never its target's, so a version whose constant targets a missing or unfitting port is still kept and fails its proof (A05 phases 2 and 3).
judgement.why: The constant carries an agent-declared schema rather than its target's schema, and constants participate in the flow-version identity.
